references.text: The Ten Commandments include the command to keep the Sabbath holy, which is the basis for the Sabbath law in Exodus 31:14.
Repeats the Sabbath command and the death penalty for those who work on the Sabbath.
Command to keep the Sabbaths as part of the holiness code.
The Sabbath is mentioned as the first of the Lord's feasts, a holy assembly.
An example of a man who was stoned for gathering wood on the Sabbath, illustrating the death penalty mentioned in Exodus 31:14.
The Sabbath command repeated in Deuteronomy with emphasis on keeping the day holy.
The prophet Isaiah speaks about the blessing of keeping the Sabbath and not profaning it.
Promise of blessing for those who keep the Sabbath holy and do not dishonor it.
Ezekiel describes the Sabbath as a sign between God and Israel, warning against profaning it.
Accusation against Jerusalem for profaning the Sabbaths.
Nehemiah warns the people against profaning the Sabbath and reminds them of God's wrath over Sabbath-breaking.
Jeremiah warns against carrying burdens on the Sabbath, with a promise of blessing or judgment.
The Epistle to the Hebrews speaks of a Sabbath rest awaiting God's people, linking it to the original Sabbath order.
Jesus discusses the meaning of the Sabbath and declares that the Son of Man is Lord of the Sabbath.
Jesus says that the Sabbath was made for man's sake, and that the Son of Man is Lord of the Sabbath.
Direct repetition of the same legal provision and death penalty for Sabbath-breaking in two different parts of Exodus.
The fundamental Sabbath commandment in Exodus 20:8 is elaborated by the consequences in Exodus 31:14.
Prophetic elaboration showing the blessing for those who keep the Sabbath, in contrast to the punishment for desecration.
Prophetic confirmation of the practical requirements of the Sabbath law and reference to the fathers' commandment.
Connects the holiness of the Sabbath to reverence for God's sanctuary and explains the gravity of breaking it.
The historical introduction and practical observance of Sabbath rest before the law was given at the mountain.
